rules.title: RSO automatic annual rent increase of 1% to 4% (CPI-based)
rules.requirement: For units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance, rent may be increased without Rent Adjustment Commission or Rent Stabilization Division permission by 1% to 4% every 12 months. The percentage is based on the 12-month CPI average ending September 30. The adjustment may be applied once each year and is not cumulative or retroactive.

rules.requirement: The calculated annual rent increase percentage for RSO units is 3%, effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

rules.title: RSO security deposit increase tied to annual rent increase
rules.requirement: For RSO units, the security deposit may be increased by 1% to 4%, at the same time and by the same percentage as the annual rent increase.

rules.requirement: Effective February 2, 2026, no rent increase is permitted when an additional dependent is added to the tenancy of an RSO unit.

rules.title: RSO increase of up to 10% per additional non-dependent tenant
rules.requirement: For additional tenants who are not dependents, the landlord may increase the rent by 10% for each such additional tenant, and the security deposit may also be increased by 10%. The bulletin lists this under the Feb. 2, 2026 item, but the 10% provision itself carries no separate effective date in the text.

rules.title: Notice of additional-tenant rent increase within 60 days
rules.requirement: The landlord must notify the tenants of the rent increase for an additional tenant within 60 days of obtaining actual or constructive knowledge of the new tenant.

rules.title: Rent reduction when additional tenant vacates
rules.requirement: A corresponding rent reduction is required when an additional tenant, whose addition supported a rent increase, vacates the unit.

rules.title: Written notice for rent increases: 30 days (under 10%) or 90 days (over 10%)
rules.requirement: Landlords must serve tenants a written 30-day notice for rent increases of less than 10% of the tenant's rent, or a 90-day notice for increases over 10% of the tenant's rent within a 12-month period.
rules.citation: LAHD Rent Stabilization Bulletin, Allowable Rent Increase (#3 – 02/02/2026), notice paragraph following item 7

rules.interaction: The bulletin does not say whether this notice requirement is limited to RSO units, so the RSO coverage is a conservative assumption. Review is needed.

rules.title: Rent to new tenant must remain the same after most vacancies
rules.requirement: For RSO units, rent to a new tenant must remain the same if the vacancy occurred for any reason other than the listed exceptions. Examples where rent may not be raised include evictions for owner or family or resident-manager occupancy, illegal use (unless based on law enforcement information), refusal to sign a new compliant rental agreement, and refusal of reasonable access.
rules.citation: LAHD Rent Stabilization Bulletin, Allowable Rent Increase (#3 – 02/02/2026), Rent Level After a Vacancy
rules.quoted_span: The RSO requires the rent to a new tenant to remain the same, if the vacancy occurred for any
rules.exemptions: Rent may be raised to any amount on re-rental if the tenant voluntarily vacated; was evicted for non-payment of legal rent; was evicted for violating the rental agreement and failing to cure; or signed a Disclosure Notice filed with LAHD and then a cash-for-keys agreement under the Tenant Buyout Notification Program (LAMC Section 151.31). The mobile home park new-tenant case is limited to 10% or the highest comparable rent, whichever is lower.

warnings: Source is an LAHD informational bulletin (#3 – 02/02/2026), not the ordinance text. No LAMC section is cited for the rent increase rules, so citations point to the bulletin only. Verify against the ordinance.
The bulletin states laws are frequently amended. Status in_force as of 2026-10-01 is assumed from the bulletin's stated dates, and no later changes were checked.

RSO coverage is represented only by legal_city and city_rent_controlled. Unit-level RSO exemptions (for example year built or certificate of occupancy) are not stated in this chunk and are not encoded.
The additional-dependent and additional-tenant triggers cannot be expressed with the allowed coverage fields and are described only in requirement text.

The 10% additional-tenant rent increase and the 60-day notice have no separate effective date in the text. Feb. 2, 2026 is applied because they sit under item 4, which begins 'Effective February 2, 2026'. Verify.
